# Dockerfile Guidelines (Alpine Linux and Ubuntu)
https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/

## Purpose
Rules for writing and reviewing Dockerfiles, `.dockerignore` and Compose files. Targets:
- **Alpine Linux 3.24** (`alpine:3.24`) — small images, musl libc, `apk`.
- **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS "Resolute Raccoon"** (`ubuntu:26.04`, supported until April 2031) — glibc, `apt`, best compatibility.
- **Slim Debian**

Build with BuildKit (default in current Docker) and write Dockerfiles that also work with Podman/Buildah.

## Choosing the base image
- Use **Alpine** for small, self-contained runtimes: static binaries, Go, Rust (musl target), Node.js, simple services and tools.
- Use **Ubuntu** when you need glibc compatibility (Python wheels with native code, .NET, Java, CUDA/ROCm, vendor binaries), `apt` packages not in Alpine, or long-term enterprise support.
- Consider Ubuntu Chiseled images or `scratch`/distroless for the final stage when the app needs no shell or package manager.
- Prefer an official language image built on these bases (`node:<ver>-alpine3.24`, `python:<ver>-slim` / Ubuntu-based, `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/*:<ver>-noble|resolute`) over installing runtimes yourself.
- Never use the `latest` tag. Pin the major/minor tag **and** the digest: `FROM alpine:3.24@sha256:<digest>`, `FROM ubuntu:26.04@sha256:<digest>`. Let Dependabot/Renovate update digests.
- Use the same base family in build and runtime stages (don't build against glibc and run on musl).

## File structure
- First line: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` to get current Dockerfile features.
- Multi-stage builds: a `build` stage with compilers and dev dependencies, a small `runtime` stage with only what the app needs. Name every stage (`FROM ... AS build`).
- Order instructions from least to most frequently changing: base, system packages, dependency manifests, dependency install, source code, build.
- Copy dependency manifests first (`package.json` + lock file, `*.csproj`, `requirements.txt`, `go.mod`) and install before copying the rest, to maximize layer caching.
- Use `COPY`, not `ADD` (except `ADD --checksum=` for verified remote files or `ADD` of a git repository with a pinned commit).
- Use `COPY --link` and `COPY --chown=<user>:<group>` instead of separate `chown` layers.
- Use `WORKDIR` with absolute paths; never `RUN cd ...`.
- Use `ARG` for build-time values (versions), `ENV` only for runtime configuration. Never put secrets in either.
- Add OCI labels: `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `.version`, `.revision`, `.licenses`, `.description`.

## Alpine (`apk`)
- Install in one `RUN` with no cache and virtual packages for build dependencies:
  ```dockerfile
  RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tzdata \
   && apk add --no-cache --virtual .build-deps build-base \
   && make -C /src \
   && apk del .build-deps
  ```
- Or use a BuildKit cache mount instead of `--no-cache` in build stages: `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apk apk add ...`.
- Pin package versions only when reproducibility requires it (`pkg~=1.2`); pinned versions disappear when Alpine updates, so prefer pinning the base image digest.
- Remember musl differences: DNS resolution, locale support and some prebuilt binaries behave differently. Test on Alpine; switch to Ubuntu if glibc is required rather than installing `gcompat` hacks.
- Busybox provides `sh`, not `bash`. Use `/bin/sh` syntax in `RUN`, or install `bash` explicitly only when needed.
- Add `tzdata` when the app needs time zones and `ca-certificates` for TLS.

## Ubuntu (`apt`)
- Install in one `RUN` with no recommended packages and clean up in the same layer:
  ```dockerfile
  RUN apt-get update \
   && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl \
   && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  ```
- Or use cache mounts in build stages: `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ...` (remove `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/docker-clean` first).
- Use `apt-get`, not `apt`, in scripts. Never run `apt-get upgrade` / `dist-upgrade` in Dockerfiles; rebuild on a newer base digest instead.
- Set `ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` (as `ARG`, not `ENV`) to avoid prompts.
- Add third-party repositories with a signed key in `/etc/apt/keyrings/` and `signed-by=`; never `apt-key`.
- Ubuntu 26.04 uses the Rust-based coreutils (uutils) by default; don't rely on obscure GNU-only flags in `RUN` scripts without testing.
- The `ubuntu` image already contains a non-root `ubuntu` user (UID 1000); reuse it or create your own with a fixed UID.

## Security
- Run as a non-root user with a fixed UID/GID (e.g. 10001): create it in the Dockerfile and set `USER` before `ENTRYPOINT`.
  - Alpine: `RUN addgroup -S -g 10001 app && adduser -S -D -H -u 10001 -G app app`
  - Ubuntu: `RUN groupadd -r -g 10001 app && useradd -r -u 10001 -g app -M -s /usr/sbin/nologin app`
- Never put secrets in `ARG`, `ENV`, `COPY`'d files or layers. Use BuildKit secrets (`RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc ...`) and SSH mounts (`--mount=type=ssh`) at build time, and runtime secrets from the orchestrator.
- Install only what's needed; no compilers, package managers' caches, `curl`/`wget` or shells in the runtime stage unless required.
- Verify downloaded files with checksums or signatures (`ADD --checksum=sha256:...`).
- Make the application filesystem read-only where possible (files owned by root, readable by the app user); write only to dedicated volumes or `/tmp`.
- Scan images in CI (Docker Scout, Trivy or Grype) and fail on critical vulnerabilities; generate an SBOM and provenance attestation (`docker buildx build --sbom=true --provenance=mode=max`).
- Don't expose unnecessary ports; never run `sshd` in a container.

## Runtime behavior
- Use exec form for `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD` (`["app", "--flag"]`) so signals reach the process; use `ENTRYPOINT` for the executable and `CMD` for default arguments.
- Make sure PID 1 handles signals and reaps children: use `docker run --init` / Compose `init: true`, or `tini` when needed.
- Log to stdout/stderr, not files.
- Add a `HEALTHCHECK` (or define probes in the orchestrator) that uses a tool present in the image.
- Declare `EXPOSE` for documentation and `STOPSIGNAL` if the app needs a signal other than `SIGTERM`.
- Configure via environment variables; provide sensible defaults and fail fast on missing required values.
- Set `TZ` and locale explicitly only when the app needs them; default to UTC.

## .dockerignore
- Always present. Exclude `.git`, `.github`, `node_modules`, build output (`bin/`, `obj/`, `dist/`), local env files (`.env*`), logs, IDE folders, tests and docs not needed in the image.
- Prefer an allow-list style (`*` then `!src/`, `!package.json`, ...) for small images.

## Compose files
- Use `compose.yaml` (no `version:` key). Pin image tags and digests as in Dockerfiles.
- Set `user`, `read_only: true`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]` and resource limits for services.
- Use `secrets:` and `env_file` for configuration; never inline passwords.
- Define `healthcheck` and use `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`.

## Build and CI
- Build with `docker buildx build` for multi-platform images (`--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`) and use registry or GitHub Actions cache (`--cache-to/--cache-from`).
- Lint Dockerfiles with Hadolint and `docker build --check`; fix warnings instead of ignoring them.
- Tag images with the git SHA and the semantic version; never overwrite released tags.
- Rebuild images regularly (at least weekly) to pick up base image security updates.

## Code review focus
Flag in this order: secrets in layers, `ARG` or `ENV`, running as root, `latest` or unpinned base images, missing `.dockerignore`, build tools or caches left in the runtime image, `apt-get upgrade`, package installs split across layers without cleanup, shell-form `ENTRYPOINT`/`CMD`, missing health checks, mixing musl (Alpine) and glibc (Ubuntu) artifacts.
